subject: gov.policy
name: Broadband and broadcasting universal access strategy
status: Discontinued, its period expired with no located renewal
milestone: Covered 2018 to 2021
position_end: The regulator's own strategy for 2018 to 2021 is the most substantive broadband instrument held, and it states that national broadband targets awaited a separate National Broadband Plan and Strategy, substituting SADC targets in the meantime; neither that plan nor a renewal is held
note: Held as an excerpt truncated within the strategic objectives

subject: gov.policy
name: Central bank annual integrated reports
milestone: Successor edition for 2025/26 acquired
position_end: Two consecutive annual integrated reports are now held, 2024/25 and 2025/26, giving the base the central bank's own account of the payment switch and its digital programme across two years rather than at second hand
note: the 2025/26 edition supersedes a payment-switch participation series the base carried from earlier reporting, which is the reason for holding both

subject: gov.policy
name: Digital Readiness Assessment
milestone: Launched November 2024 by the ICT ministry with a development agency
position_end: Published, placing the country at the systematic stage across all six pillars - digital public infrastructure, connectivity, government, regulation, economy and people - and finding only moderate political support for digitalisation despite a national strategy being in place

subject: gov.policy
name: National Data Governance Policy
milestone: ICT minister told the Senate the policy is targeted for completion before end-2026, with government undecided between a standalone data-governance law and amendments to existing legislation
position_start: Being procured through a Smart Africa tender (2025-07)
position_end: Validated; targeted for completion before the end of the year, and drafted for 2027 to 2031 on a tell-government-once principle under which a citizen supplies information once and authorised institutions reach it when delivering a service
note: Minister's completion target was stated as aspirational (hoping, planning) in Senate debate, not a statutory deadline.

subject: gov.policy
name: National information and communication infrastructure policy
milestone: Adopted by Cabinet August 2006
position_end: The 2006 policy is the identifiable national ICT policy, with an implementation plan drafted for 2012 to 2016 and no located replacement; the ICT ministry's own report to Parliament for 2024/25 still runs against it
note: Held as an excerpt truncated partway through section 1.2

subject: gov.policy
name: Science, technology and innovation policy review and 4IR/5IR strategy
milestone: Stakeholder validation opened 2026-02-24
position_end: The ICT ministry's research and innovation department opened stakeholder validation of a reviewed national science, technology and innovation policy together with a combined fourth and fifth industrial revolution strategy, presented as a re-engineering of national systems around a human-centred economy; neither document is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Access to Information Bill
milestone: A departmental action-plan item, not tabled
position_start: Named as an action-plan item and not tabled
position_end: Named as an action-plan item and not tabled
note: A media-freedom body said in February 2026 it was on standby to support enactment; the ministry reaffirmed cooperation and made no enactment commitment

subject: gov.legislate
name: Critical Infrastructure Protection Bill
milestone: Bill No. 16 of 2025, resumed in the Senate 2026-02-26
position_end: The Senate moved to suspend its standing orders and take the Bill at the stage it had reached in the preceding session, sponsored by the ICT minister; no Act, commencement or text is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybersecurity, critical infrastructure, e-commerce and AI legislation
milestone: Named as forthcoming alongside the Mbabane smart-city deployment
position_end: Announced as forthcoming; no bill text or tabling date on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Communications and Transactions Act, 2022
milestone: Act No. 3 of 2022
position_end: The operative electronic-transactions statute, and the closest instrument to a legal basis for data exchange between public bodies; the base holds no Act creating an interoperability duty

subject: gov.legislate
name: Licence-exempt spectrum guidelines
milestone: Issued under section 38(b) of the ESCCOM Act
position_end: The regulator's 2024 guidelines on licence-exempt spectrum bands are the base's only binding instrument expressly touching artificial-intelligence and internet-of-things devices; there is no artificial-intelligence Act or regulation

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Payment Systems Regulations, 2026
status: Planned, approved by Cabinet and not confirmed gazetted
milestone: Cabinet approval reported for the first quarter of 2026/27
position_end: Cabinet approved regulations to operationalise the 2023 Act as part of a wider reform package; no gazette text, publication or commencement date is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Payments System Act, 2023
milestone: Act No. 5 of 2023
position_end: In force: the regulation and supervision of payment systems, the safety and efficiency of the national payments system, and the central bank's functions in relation to them

subject: gov.legislate
name: Online Media Publishing Guidelines 2026
milestone: Ministry stated development is complete
position_end: Complete on the ministry's account, introducing publisher registration and rules on accuracy, privacy, child safeguarding and the responsible use of AI; text and commencement date not public

subject: gov.legislate
name: Ratification of the cyber and data protection conventions
milestone: Presented to senators 2026-07-10
position_end: The ICT minister presented the African Union Malabo Convention on cyber security and personal data protection, the Budapest Convention on cybercrime and the Tampere Convention to senators for ratification; SADC ICT ministers urged member states to consider ratifying Malabo in September 2019, and no instrument of ratification is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statistics Act, 1967
milestone: Act 14 of 1967
position_end: The operative statute constituting the Central Statistical Office and carrying its collection powers, unamended on the base and now fifty-nine years old; no replacement Bill or commencement is held

subject: gov.protect
name: Advisory guidelines on processing personal health data
milestone: Validation workshops opened at Ezulwini
position_end: In validation; to be published as a regulatory instrument under the Data Protection Act

subject: gov.protect
name: Biometric gate passes in schools
milestone: Deployed by some public schools without education ministry approval, at about E200 per pupil
position_end: Deployed and refused by some teachers and parents on consent and child-data grounds

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Protection Act 2022
milestone: Gazetted and effective 4 March 2022
position_end: In force; fines to E5,000,000 or 2% of annual turnover
sources: 2022-03-04 Eswatini Data Protection Act 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022)
note: The gazetted text names a Data Protection Commission; ESCCOM's own pages describe it as the designated Data Protection Agency. The mismatch is recorded, not resolved.

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Protection Act applied to online naming and shaming
milestone: Exposure to a E100,000 penalty reported 2026-08-16
position_start: No application of the Act to personal online posting held
position_end: A social-media practice of publicly naming individuals over alleged private conduct is reported as exposing posters to a penalty of up to E100,000 under the Data Protection Act 2022
sources: 2026-08-16-eswatiniobserver-data-protection-act-online-shaming|2022-03-04 Eswatini Data Protection Act 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022)
note: a press account of legal exposure rather than an enforcement action; no complaint, ruling or authority statement is held

subject: gov.protect
name: Enforcement notices under the Data Protection Act
milestone: Listed on the authority's enforcement page
position_end: Three notices published under section 41 of the Act - two in June 2024 against a mobile operator and an insurer, and one in March 2025 against the science and technology park
note: The notices themselves are downloadable documents; the page carries no register of complaints or breach notifications

subject: gov.protect
name: Eswatini Data Protection Authority
milestone: Opened its first major investigation, into the Ministry of Home Affairs
position_start: Office not operationalised three years after the Act took effect (2025-07)
position_end: Operating: an awareness campaign, a registration deadline of 31 March 2026, one concluded complaint and one investigation into a ministry
sources: 2026-06-24-home-affairs-investigated-for-sensitive-data-breach|2026-02-03-eswatini-launches-data-protection-campaign|2025-07-31 Eswatini Economic Update - Digital Transformation Key to Unlocking Growth

subject: gov.protect
name: Home Affairs publication of unblurred national identity documents
milestone: Investigation opened; the ministry missed the 72-hour breach-notification duty
position_end: Under investigation by the data protection authority

subject: gov.protect
name: Mandatory data mapping and inventory directive
milestone: General Notice 2 of 2025; inventories due 31 March 2026
position_end: Every data controller and processor, public bodies included, must map and inventory its data — flows, storage location and sharing — under section 14 of the Data Protection Act; no compliance count is held
note: Held as an excerpt truncated by the source document's own extraction

subject: gov.protect
name: Restrictions on children's access to social media
milestone: Raised in Senate; ministries stated to be working on online-content regulation (2026-08)
position_end: Under consideration only: two ministries stated to be working on online-content regulation in answer to a Senate question, with no bill, mechanism or age threshold named
note: a senator asked during the Senate debate on the Deputy Prime Minister's Office first-quarter performance report what prevents minors reaching harmful content; the answer, given for the tourism ministry, was that the Deputy Prime Minister's Office is working with the ICT ministry on online-content regulation. No instrument, timetable, age-verification method or definition of harmful content is stated, and the base holds no draft

subject: gov.protect
name: Sector data-protection guidelines
milestone: Draft guidelines validated at a week-long workshop, 2026-08-11
position_end: Draft sector guidelines under the Data Protection Act 2022 validated at a week-long workshop, which also produced a proposed whistle-blower-protection framework; the regulator used it to name the financial sector as the leading source of personal-data breaches, through misdirected statements and invoices and cybersecurity incidents exposing customer records
note: no breach count, penalty or enforcement action is published behind the regulator's ranking, and the draft guidelines are not held

subject: gov.protect
name: United States bilateral health agreement and its data-sharing agreement
milestone: Memorandum announced 2026-08-18
position_end: A health-funding memorandum with the United States worth more than 3.24 billion emalangeni, about US$195 million, announced during a call by a State Department official on the prime minister under a bilateral global health strategy
note: a federal complaint filed 2026-04-02 records that the State Department entered into dozens of such bilateral agreements between December 2025 and February 2026, each typically a memorandum plus at least one further agreement on data sharing, that a FOIA request of 2025-12-20 covers the Eswatini agreements, and that the department published a subset of the memoranda in March 2026 and then withdrew public access; the data-sharing terms remain unpublished

subject: gov.regional
name: Chairmanship of the SADC Organ on Politics, Defence and Security
milestone: Elected at the 46th summit, Durban, 17 August 2026
position_end: The King was elected Chairperson of the Organ on Politics, Defence and Security Cooperation at the 46th ordinary summit; no digital or ICT portfolio attaches to the role on the base

subject: gov.regional
name: Regional federated e-KYC framework
milestone: Grant partnership announced August 2025 to build the framework across 16 member states
position_end: Technical assistance funded to connect national digital identity systems into a federated know-your-customer layer over the regional settlement and immediate-clearing payment systems
note: Announced by the implementing partners rather than by the regional secretariat; no Eswatini-specific commitment, date or instrument is named

subject: gov.regional
name: SADC adequacy model for cross-border data transfers
milestone: Transfers within SADC permitted under conditions by the Data Protection Act 2022
position_end: In force
sources: 2022-03-04 Eswatini Data Protection Act 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022)

subject: gov.regional
name: SADC ICT ministerial participation
milestone: Endorsed the draft SADC Digital Transformation Strategy, June 2023
position_end: Eswatini attended the September 2019 ministerial, which approved mobile broadband gap analysis guidelines and a framework for a regional computer incident response team and urged ratification of the Malabo Convention, and the June 2023 ministerial, which endorsed the draft SADC Digital Transformation Strategy and approved the SADC Postal Strategy 2022-2025

subject: gov.standards
name: Designation of national standards
milestone: Nineteen standards designated by General Notice 79 of 2025
position_end: Nineteen new national standards were designated across electricity, fuel facilities, liquefied petroleum gas, food production, beverages, climate change adaptation and household consumer products, and construction began in December 2025 on certification cottage factories at Lugongolweni for a micro-enterprise conformity scheme

subject: gov.standards
name: Division of the data-protection mandate
milestone: ICT ministry stated on the record that implementation, enforcement and oversight are vested in ESCCOM, not itself
position_end: Executive holds policy, ESCCOM holds implementation, enforcement and oversight; no third institution named

subject: gov.standards
name: Information technology standards catalogue
milestone: 28 information-technology standards listed
position_end: The standards authority's information-technology catalogue lists 28 standards domesticated under the SZNS designation, among them the ISO records-management standard and the Dublin Core metadata element set

subject: gov.standards
name: National addressing standards
milestone: Launched 20 July 2026 with two municipal pilots
position_end: The Eswatini National Addressing Standards, the ISO 19160 parts 1 and 2 domesticated as SZNS, launched by the standards authority with the communications regulator and the ICT and housing ministries; Mbabane is leading a national street addressing and house numbering programme and Ezulwini is among the pilot municipalities

subject: gov.standards
name: Quality certification of the revenue service
milestone: Certified to SZNS ISO 9001
position_end: The national standards authority certified the revenue service to the domesticated ISO 9001 quality management standard
note: The record is the standards authority's own announcement on a social platform

subject: gov.standards
name: Standards and Quality Act
milestone: Act 10 of 2003, assented 8 November 2001
position_end: The statute constituting the national standards authority; a 2025 account of new designations cites a later Standards and Quality Act of 2023 as the enabling statute, and that Act is not held

subject: gov.discourse
name: National Cybersecurity Advisory Council
milestone: Provided for by the Computer Crime and Cybercrime Act, 2022
position_end: Provided for by the Act as the standing body through which interests outside government reach cybersecurity governance; no appointment, membership or meeting record is held

subject: gov.discourse
name: National data policy consultation
milestone: Drafting workshop April 2026; validation workshop July 2026
position_end: A two-day stakeholders' workshop opened on 29 April 2026 with European Union, member state and GIZ support began drafting the national data policy, and a validation workshop in July 2026 put the draft to government ministries, regulators, the private sector, civil society, academia and development partners

subject: gov.discourse
name: Public account of the Google memorandum
milestone: Prime minister first dismissed the memorandum, then acknowledged in writing that Cabinet had approved it
position_end: Established after a public contradiction between the prime minister and the Attorney-General

subject: finance.budget
name: Domestic budget appropriation for digital transformation
milestone: No estimates volume or appropriation line on file for the ICT ministry, ESCCOM or RSTP
position_end: Not held

subject: finance.budget
name: Tax gap
milestone: Stated by the revenue commissioner general at the filing season launch
position_end: E4.4 billion, wholesale and retail the largest contributor, chiefly in value added tax (2025-10)

subject: finance.mou
name: Global South Utilities discussions on data-centre power
milestone: Met at the World Government Summit; nothing signed
position_end: In discussion; no capacity, price or timetable stated

subject: finance.new
name: Digital Eswatini Project
milestone: More than E1.06bn of World Bank financing approved, reported at US$65m
position_end: Approved: E648m for broadband and E450m for Government In Your Hand, with a 2027 rollout
note: Converted in the source at E16.37 to US$1 (2026-07-19); the ministry's own quarterly report behind it is not held.

subject: finance.new
name: Private sponsorship of trade fair connectivity
milestone: E570,000 for the 2026 fair, a third consecutive year
position_end: A domestic internet provider put E570,000 into free wireless access across the nine-day national trade fair, its third consecutive year as official sponsor

subject: finance.new
name: Taiwan-funded smart city expansion
milestone: Memorandum signed alongside the 2026 Smart City Summit in Taipei
position_end: The ICT minister signed a memorandum with a Taiwanese systems integrator extending the 5G government network smart city project from a Mbabane pilot to Manzini and Matsapha, stated as fully funded by the government of Taiwan; no commitment amount, timetable or camera count is given
note: No deal record was built: the source states no figure, so it fails the finance branch's five-fact test on amount

subject: finance.new
name: World Bank digital-transformation opportunity
milestone: Noted as omitted from the prime minister's 2025 year-end statement
position_end: US$165m, equivalent to E2.8bn, identified and unaddressed in the year-end statement

subject: infra.connect
name: Backbone access and facilities-sharing ruling
milestone: Notice 5 of 2026, effective 1 July 2026
position_end: On the national operator's complaint that a private provider had built its own cross-border fibre link from a border post and bypassed the national backbone, the regulator fined the provider E150,000 and directed the national operator to give reliable, non-discriminatory and transparent backbone access and to share its existing connections and fibre topology with internet service providers, with service levels, pricing and complaint routes disclosed

subject: infra.connect
name: Cost of data as a share of income per head
milestone: Above the international affordability threshold
position_end: 3.47% of gross national income per head

subject: infra.connect
name: Cross-border backbone redundancy route
milestone: A universal access fund project with the national backbone operator
position_end: An alternative cross-border route to Maputo over powerline fibre and onward to undersea-cable access at Cape Town, begun by the universal access fund with the national operator in response to frequent backbone and internet failures
note: Held as an excerpt truncated within a later sub-project description

subject: infra.connect
name: Mbabane smart-city deployment
milestone: 5G network, 59 AI-enabled cameras and public Wi-Fi being fitted in the capital
position_end: Under installation; no completion date published

subject: infra.connect
name: Minimum internet service standard
milestone: ESCCOM proposed raising the minimum from 2 Mbps to 10 Mbps in Notice 08/2026
position_end: 10 Mbps proposed; the 2 Mbps standard remains in force

subject: infra.connect
name: Mobile coverage against mobile-internet use
milestone: Ministry of ICT figures given at the Digital Eswatini change-management workshop
position_start: About 95% 4G coverage against about 58% internet use
position_end: 95% mobile coverage against 57% mobile-internet subscription (2026-07)

subject: infra.connect
name: National fibre-optic backbone
milestone: International capacity raised from 47 to 72 Gbps, above target
position_end: 72 Gbps international capacity; rollout continuing

subject: infra.connect
name: National internet exchange point
milestone: Launched 10 April 2014 under the African Union's exchange-point project
position_end: Launched by the African Union Commission with the ICT ministry and the Internet Society to keep intra-country traffic inside the country; no peering-member count, traffic figure or operating statement later than the launch is held

subject: infra.connect
name: Public-institution connectivity programme
milestone: 1,031 institutions targeted under the Digital Eswatini Project
position_end: 859 schools, 134 health facilities and 38 tinkhundla centres to be connected

subject: infra.connect
name: Statutory complaint adjudication by ESCCOM
milestone: Free adjudication under the Eswatini Communications Commission Act 2013, with windows of one month for post and courier, three for broadcasting and six for telecommunications
position_end: In force
note: Structural provisions of the Act, not dated state.

subject: infra.store
name: National Data Centre
milestone: Government assessment finds ministries depend heavily on it with no internal fallback
position_start: Operating; no capacity, tenant, uptime tier or utilisation disclosed
position_end: Operating and named a structural concentration risk; still no capacity, tenant, uptime tier or utilisation on file
sources: 2026-05-21-critical-state-information-at-risk-in-9-govt-ministries|2021-01-01 The National Data Centre - Royal Science and Technology Park

subject: infra.store
name: National data centre disaster recovery site
milestone: E58m allocated in 2021; consultancy tendered October 2025
position_start: Construction begun at KaLanga with E58 million allocated (2021-02)
position_end: Five years after the allocation the site is not recorded as operating, and the communications regulator went out to tender in October 2025 for consultancy services on a data centre disaster recovery facility
note: Financed by a US$10.4m India Exim Bank line of credit signed in 2021 for the science park's second phase

subject: infra.energy
name: Electricity tariff structure
milestone: Revised tariff effective 1 April 2026
position_end: An average increase of 13.61% approved for 2026/27 and revised down to 11.74% after special government funding, with a lifeline domestic band and time-of-use commercial tariffs; no data-centre or large-load category appears anywhere in the schedule
note: A rural electrification levy of 2.5% of the energy charge is included in every category

subject: infra.energy
name: Electrification rate
position_end: 88 per cent at the 2024/25 year end, on 298,918 customers and 126 MW of installed capacity

subject: infra.energy
name: Power supply to the National Data Centre
milestone: ICT minister met an Abu Dhabi clean-energy firm to discuss dedicated supply; nothing signed
position_end: Still being sourced five years after the facility opened; no capacity, price or timetable stated

subject: infra.energy
name: Rural network reinforcement and energy access programme
milestone: 5,600 of 8,000 targeted connections at October 2025; closing December 2025
position_end: 5,600 of 8,000 targeted household connections in the Shiselweni region at October 2025, 70 per cent, with 6,500 sought by the project's December closure and the remainder carried forward into a successor project aiming at universal access by 2030
note: The project disbursed its full EUR 35.7m and was rated satisfactory at the mission

subject: infra.capacity
name: Compute or high-performance computing capacity
milestone: The National Data Centre states high-performance computing as an objective but discloses no capacity
position_end: Not held

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Government services available online
milestone: Digital Landscape Assessment count
position_end: 31 of 419 services online; 15 of 22 ministries run on 1 Mbps or less; 18 ICT professionals support the assessed estate

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Ministry data backup and ICT maintenance
milestone: Digital Landscape Assessment received and endorsed by the ICT ministry
position_end: 9 of 21 ministries keep no regular backups, 11 have no ICT maintenance contract, and the finance ministry runs mainframe software past end of life

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National cybersecurity awareness programme
milestone: Cybersecurity Awareness Month opened by the prime minister
position_end: Run annually; no national cybersecurity strategy or CERT on file

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Police Digital Forensic Unit and cyber task team
milestone: 87 arrests made and 528 dockets submitted to the prosecutions director
position_end: In operation against mobile money fraud, fake wallet schemes, online loan scams and rental scams, with 87 arrests and 528 dockets submitted

subject: infra.cybersec
name: SADC regional cybersecurity framework
milestone: Finalised and approved by the SADC Committee of Central Bank Governors subcommittee at Ezulwini
position_end: Approved regionally; no national implementing instrument on file

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Value involved in cyber-related crime
milestone: Police figure for the twelve months to 30 September 2025
position_end: Over E8.5 million, 1 September 2024 to 30 September 2025

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Government system interoperability
milestone: Digital Landscape Assessment finding
position_end: More than half of ministries lack meaningful interoperability or central-repository connectivity

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Health information exchange and master patient index
milestone: Two implementation phases completed by an external partner
position_end: A master patient index with deterministic and probabilistic matching, integrated with the population registry, feeding an interoperability platform that exchanges clinical and demographic data in a health data standard
note: Built and documented by an implementing partner rather than the ministry; no statement of which facilities are connected or what volume is exchanged

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Mchumanisi national data exchange platform
milestone: Proposed in the draft data governance policy for 2027-2031
position_end: Proposed as the platform through which authorised institutions would reach information a citizen supplies once, on a tell-government-once principle, with birth and marriage certificate services named among the intended uses; no specification, procurement or timetable is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Revenue service data matching across government databases
milestone: Compliance improvement plan launched with the 2025 filing season
position_end: A digital transformation agenda integrating national databases for data matching, with taxpayers segmented four ways and analytics and fiscalisation tools named as the detection method

subject: dpi.id
name: Birth registration at the point of birth
milestone: Registration offices open in seven towns
position_end: Under the Civil Registration Act of 2023 the Closing of the Tap initiative registers newborns directly inside health facilities, with registration offices open in seven towns; no count of births registered through it is held
note: The domain is new to the base; the page carries no day-level byline and the date is taken from its metadata

subject: dpi.id
name: Digital identity
milestone: Electronic IDs planned under the Digital Eswatini Project for a 2027 rollout
position_end: Planned under the Digital Eswatini Project; nothing issued
sources: 2026-06-24-ict-trains-change-agents-e1-2bn-digitization|2024-11-22 Eswatini unveils readiness report for digital ID, transformation push

subject: dpi.id
name: National e-KYC registry
milestone: Central bank standing it up to digitise identity verification
position_end: Under construction, with a SADC cross-border dimension; the FinTech Strategy targets 500,000 users by 2028

subject: dpi.id
name: National identity card
milestone: Production resumed February 2026; chief-code verification campaign August 2026
position_end: Production resumed at ten service centres in February 2026 after a suspension for technical upgrades, with a plan to clear the backlog; in August 2026 the ministry asked citizens to check that the chief code on their identity documents matches their actual chiefdom, warning that a wrong code obstructs access to government services. The card does not meet the criteria for digital identification
sources: 2026-08-18-home-affairs-chief-codes-verification|2026-02-23-id-card-services-resume|2026-02-22-home-affairs-resumes-id-card-production|2024-07-22 Risk of human rights infringement as Eswatini rushes to regulate the ICT sector

subject: dpi.id
name: Unique identification number issued at birth
milestone: Confirmed in a seven-country regional scoping study, April 2026
position_end: A unique identification number is issued at birth and appears on both the birth-registration record and the birth certificate, which is the link between civil registration and the national population register
note: The same study finds registrars in some of the seven countries making a citizenship determination at the point of birth registration

subject: dpi.pay
name: Bank transaction charges
milestone: Finance portfolio committee report tabled
position_end: A withdrawal of E4,000 attracting E79 to E89 in fees (2026-07)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cash share of person-to-business payments
milestone: World Bank assessment
position_end: More than 90% still cash-based (2025-08)
sources: 2025-08-05 Robust DPI inevitable for Eswatini's economic, jobs boom - World Bank

subject: dpi.pay
name: Comparative benchmark of bank charges
milestone: Portfolio committee recommended the central bank report within 30 days of adoption
position_end: Recommended, benchmarked against SACU and Common Monetary Area banks

subject: dpi.pay
name: Digital currency design paper
milestone: Design paper published 2024
position_end: The central bank's own design document for a digital national currency, now held where the base had carried only later reports naming it
note: a design paper is not an issuance decision; no pilot, launch date or governance arrangement follows it here

subject: dpi.pay
name: Eswatini Payment Switch
milestone: Fast Payments launched at Ezulwini, phase one of three
position_start: Fast Payments live with three of eight integrating participants
position_end: Fast Payments live; open banking and card, point-of-sale and ATM switching still to come
sources: 2025-01-14 Phil Mnisi - Eswatini Payment Switch Fast Payments product launch|2025-09-28-eswatini-payment-switch-explainer
note: No source held confirms whether the remaining five participants went live as expected by end-January 2025.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Interbank payment and settlement system
milestone: Rules adopted by the settlement steering committee May 2007
position_end: In operation under its 2007 rulebook
note: The rulebook has not been revised on the record since 2007; no volume or value statistic for the system is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Migration of Common Monetary Area low-value flows to TCIB
milestone: Reported as under way; no timetable, volume, value or mandating instrument given
position_end: Low-value transactions moving off domestic electronic-funds-transfer rails onto the regional scheme

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile money platform migration to a cloud-native vendor platform
milestone: Migration completed across four markets, reported 2026-08-21
position_end: The dominant operator's mobile money platform moved off a legacy virtualised environment onto a cloud-native vendor fintech platform, the vendor reporting cuts of up to 86% in CPU processing and database load and up to 80% in API response times; the migration completed in Eswatini, Ghana, Rwanda and Uganda, with Cameroon under way and Benin, the Republic of the Congo and Zambia in discussion
note: the performance figures are the vendor's own; no downtime, cost or subscriber-impact figure is stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: National FinTech Strategy 2025-2030
milestone: Launched by the central bank governor and the finance minister
position_end: In force, targeting 500,000 e-KYC users and 80% interoperability by 2028

subject: dpi.pay
name: PAPSS accession
milestone: Central bank governor discussed leveraging Egyptian experience to accelerate accession
position_end: Not a participant; no accession date, target or application status stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: Post offices as government payment points
milestone: 35 post offices opened for government-service payments
position_end: 35 post offices accepting government-service payments

subject: dpi.pay
name: Provident fund digitisation
milestone: Paperless, with a client data-cleaning exercise begun
position_end: The national provident fund reports going paperless and beginning a know-your-customer data-cleaning exercise on client records ahead of conversion into a national pension scheme, which the Prime Minister said government is fully behind

subject: dpi.pay
name: Social grant disbursement system
milestone: Bank-paid elderly grants moved to the 25th from August 2026
position_end: A disbursement system built with the science park moved bank-paid elderly grants from the 20th to the 25th of the month, presented as making payment safer, faster and more reliable; no recipient count, value or failure rate is held
